label: third original token when the second token is g
explanation: Fires in the original (input) phase on the input at step t=2 when the input at t=1 was g (pattern ?, g, [here]). Every activation has prev_tok == g, and 93% of activation mass is at t=2. Weak spillover: the step after a g at t=2 (t=3, about 6% of mass) and the step after a leading g (t=1, low values). Magnitude is highest when the first token is x: x g ? fires on 100% of cases and at about 3x the mean activation. The token at t=2 also matters, with r strongest. Precision is about 0.77 because some ?-g-? sequences do not fire. It never fires on the delimiter or copy phases, and never on a g that occurs later in the sequence.

issues: The false positives follow a pattern, not scattered noise. When I split the predicate (prev_tok==g)&(t==2) by first token (dev), first tokens b (precision 0.054), j (0.03) and k (0.00) almost never fire. v (0.25), d (0.31), w (0.33), m (0.36), u (0.49), a (0.57) and t (0.67) fire only part of the time. Every other first token gives precision 1.0 (2 gives 0.95). The explanation's 'some ?-g-? steps stay inactive' therefore hides a clear gate on the first token.

The explanation says adding conditions did not beat the simple predicate, but conditioning on first_tok does. Excluding first tokens {b,j,k} raises test F1 from 0.818 to 0.860. Excluding {b,j,k,v,d,w,m} raises test F1 to 0.879 (precision 0.945, recall 0.822, mass recall 0.928), with matching dev scores.

The label 'third original token when the second token is g' overclaims: it implies the feature fires whenever the second token is g, but for about 3 first tokens it is effectively off and for about 7 more it fires only some of the time.

These claims check out: every activation has prev_tok==g; 93.5% of mass is at t=2; spillover at t=3 is about 6% of mass and at t=1 about 0.2%; the delimiter/copy phases have essentially zero activations (1 delimiter step); x g ? has precision 1.0 with mass/recall ratio about 3.1x (test); r is the strongest in_tok.
skeptic.revised_label: third original token when the second token is g, gated by the first token (silent when the first token is b/j/k, weak for v/d/w/m/u/a/t, strongest when it is x)
